what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Programming across every channel works when they share state
sections.para: I brief by voice, review on a phone, test on a computer and read pull requests on GitHub. Rigby's 2011 omnichannel idea applies: every channel reads and writes one shared state of git, vaults, briefs and graphs. In three days, 54 messages became 40 releases, 36 articles and 87 figures.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Omnichannel, not multichannel: every channel shares one state
sections.para: Voice, chat, phone, IDE, pull request, preview and vault all share git, vaults, briefs and graphs, so switching is cheap. This site turned 54 messages into 40 releases in three days. Review is a channel too, it works at every Wardley stage, and the shared state fixes its known failures.

sections.label: Where the word comes from
sections.line: Omnichannel means one shared state, not separate copies
sections.para: Darrell Rigby introduced omnichannel retailing in Harvard Business Review in December 2011. A multichannel retailer keeps separate stock and records per channel; an omnichannel one has one customer, basket and stock. Programming became multichannel by accident, and becomes omnichannel when every channel reads and writes the same state.

sections.label: What it looks like
sections.line: A day moves between channels without copying anything across
sections.para: A walking voice memo becomes a brief, an agent pushes from the cloud, and I review on my phone and reply by voice. Tests run on the computer, diffs on GitHub, checks on an iPad, and experiments live in vaults. Claude Code reached web and iOS on 20 October 2025.

sections.label: This site, counted
sections.line: Three days turned 54 messages into 40 releases
sections.para: From 13 to 15 October 2026 the session took 54 messages, ten of them voice memos, producing 40 releases, 36 articles and 87 figures. It fetched 75 pages, ran 23 searches and started 33 background agents, with hooks, a leak scan and 16 test suites. Other sessions made 15 releases in the same repository.

sections.label: Reviewing is a channel too
sections.line: Review now happens by voice and as a graph
sections.para: Drafts are reviewed by voice, with the agent checking memory against the record. Code is reviewed as a fractal semantic graph from stories down to calls, so the review becomes programmatic; secrets.sgit.ai showed 42 claims shipped and the app still proposed. One-off interfaces are further channels into the same state.

sections.label: Every stage, every altitude
sections.line: Explorers, villagers and town planners all use every channel
sections.para: Explorers use voice for half-formed ideas and vaults for safe experiments. Villagers use voice for draft review and read code as a graph, while town planners write policies once and hold code with CI gates. When this site moved from explorer to villager, the channels stayed; their uses changed.

sections.label: The new generation already works like this
sections.line: A new generation already programs across channels by default
sections.para: In Stack Overflow's 2025 survey, 84% use or plan to use AI tools, and about half of professionals use them daily. Y Combinator said a quarter of W25 startups had 95% AI-generated code. Yet 46% distrust AI accuracy against 33% who trust it, which is why shared state matters.

sections.label: What breaks
sections.line: It fails through fragmentation, misplaced secrets and lost context
sections.para: A decision living only in one channel is invisible to the next, so nothing counts until it reaches the shared state. More channels mean more places to paste a key, hence a leak scan before every commit. Summaries drop context, so rules live in a file re-read after every summary.

sections.label: The wider claim
sections.line: Shared state extends the pattern to omnichannel computing
sections.para: Once state is shared and channels are just ways in, the pattern applies to writing, risk reviews and talks. The homepage-as-vault proposal makes each edition a commit, readable as a page, a history or a clonable folder. Vaults provide that shared state without a server that can read the data.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: One session's counts, a new term and 2025 figures
sections.para: The counts cover three days of one agent session on one site, not a study. The term omnichannel programming appears new in this sense, and the survey figures date from 2025. Some work still needs a screen, keyboard and line-by-line human review.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: Rigby, Stack Overflow, TechCrunch and Anthropic
sections.para: Written from a 15 October 2026 voice memo, with counts from the session transcript and dev branch log. Sources are Rigby's The Future of Shopping (HBR, 2011), Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, TechCrunch on YC's cohort (6 March 2025) and Anthropic's Claude Code on the web.
